chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Kufi, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, when Dawud (peace be upon him) took his stand at Arafat, he looked at the people and their multitude, so he ascended the mountain and turned to supplicate. When he had completed his rituals, Jibra'il (peace be upon him) came to him and said to him: 'O Dawud! Your Lord says to you: Why did you ascend the mountain? Did you think that the voice of one who speaks would be hidden from Me?'

Then he took him to the sea, to Jeddah, and caused him to descend into the water, traveling for forty mornings on land. Then there was a rock, which he split open, and there was a worm in it. He said to him: 'O Dawud! Your Lord says to you: I hear the voice of this one in the belly of this rock at the bottom of this sea. So did you think that the voice of one who speaks would be hidden from Me?'

key_terms.دُودَةٌ: A worm/larva, representing a small creature

ai.seo_question: What lesson did Prophet Dawud learn about God's hearing from the story of the worm in the rock?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Prophet Dawud (peace be upon him) ascends a mountain at Arafat during Hajj, perhaps seeking solitude or fearing his voice might be lost in the crowd, but God corrects this subtle assumption of concealment. Through Jibra'il, God demonstrates His absolute omniscience by revealing He hears the faintest sound of a worm inside a rock at the bottom of the sea, affirming that no voice is hidden from Him. This event underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *Ilm al-Ghayb* (Knowledge of the Unseen) belonging exclusively to God, even for the Prophets, and serves as a spiritual lesson for pilgrims to maintain sincerity (*Ikhlas*) rather than seeking physical isolation for worship.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Kufy, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Usman Bin Isa, from Ibn Muskan, from the one who reported it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When Dawood<sup>as</sup> paused at the Pausing Station in Arafat, looked at the people and their abundance. So he<sup>as</sup> climbed upon the mountain, and started supplicating. So when he<sup>as</sup> had completed his<sup>as</sup> rituals, Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> came over to him and said to him<sup>as</sup>: ‘O Dawood<sup>as</sup>! Your<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> is Saying to you<sup>as</sup>: “Why did you<sup>as</sup> ascend the mountain? Do you<sup>as</sup> think that a voice from the voices would be concealed from Me<sup>azwj</sup>?”

Then he<sup>as</sup> went with him<sup>as</sup> to the sea to Jeddah. So he<sup>as</sup> swam with him<sup>as</sup> in the sea for a travel distance of forty mornings in the land. So there was a rock, and he (Jibraeel<sup>as</sup> split it and there was an insect in it. So he<sup>as</sup> said to him<sup>as</sup>: ‘O Dawood<sup>as</sup>! Your<sup>as</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> is Saying to you<sup>as</sup>: “I<sup>azwj</sup> can Hear the voice of this one in the inside of this rock at the bottom of this sea, so do you<sup>as</sup> think that a voice from the voices would be concealed from Me<sup>azwj</sup>?”’
en.sarwar: 11. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Kufiy from Ali ibn Mahziyar from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from ibn Muskan from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

Dawud (David) stayed at the station in ‘Arafat and looked at the people who seemed of great number to him. He then climbed the hill and began to pray. When he completed that act of Hajj, Jibril came to him and said, ‘O Dawud, your Lord asks, “Why did you climb the hill? Did you think that the voice of one who calls Me (prays to Me) may remain hidden from Me?”’

He (Jibril) then took him to the sea near Jaddah. He (Jibril) made him swim underwater for a distance equal to forty mornings on land. At that point there was a rock, which he (Jibril) cut open and inside there was a little worm. He (Jibril) said, ‘O Dawud, your Lord says, “I hear the voice of this worm inside this rock in the depth of this sea, but you thought that the voice of a caller (one who prays to Me) may remain hidden and obscure before Me.’””
